title: Where a battery must not go: vehicle damage
text: A BESS must not be installed where damage from external influences may be expected, e.g. from a vehicle. Bollards or a protected position may be used to prevent vehicle contact.
source: ERAC · Battery Energy Storage System Installation Requirements (AS/NZS 5139:2019), published 2 Feb 2021, p. 2

title: Hazardous areas and gas
text: A BESS must not be installed in a hazardous area as defined in AS/NZS 3000 (Fig 4.18 distances from gas cylinders; Fig 4.19 distances from gas relief vent valves). Local gas network providers may have additional exclusion zones around gas meters. Victoria: gas distribution requirement is 1000 mm diameter from the gas meter vent to a distance of 1500 mm in the direction of discharge.
source: ERAC · Battery Energy Storage System Installation Requirements (AS/NZS 5139:2019), published 2 Feb 2021, pp. 2, 6

title: Windows and vents
text: A BESS must not be installed within 600 mm horizontally and 900 mm below an opening window to a habitable room, or vents (mechanical, electrical or other ventilation openings) to habitable rooms.
source: ERAC · Battery Energy Storage System Installation Requirements (AS/NZS 5139:2019), published 2 Feb 2021, p. 2

title: Exits, walkways, stairs and escape routes
text: A BESS must not be installed within a passageway, walkway, exit, escape or evacuation route, or underneath entrance/exit walkways, staircases and escape routes. Not within 600 mm of an exit with an opening of 900 mm or less; openings wider than 900 mm (e.g. a garage opening) must allow a person to pass more than 1000 mm from the nearest side of the BESS. NSW variation: all openings that can be used as an exit, e.g. garage or double doors, are classified as exits and a BESS shall not be installed within 600 mm of the exit.
source: ERAC · Battery Energy Storage System Installation Requirements (AS/NZS 5139:2019), published 2 Feb 2021, pp. 3, 6

title: Roofs, ceilings and wall cavities
text: A BESS must not be installed on roofs (excluding roofs accessible via a permanently installed staircase or access ladder), within ceiling spaces, or set into wall cavities. A recess entirely sealed to the cavity with non-combustible material, or a separate non-combustible enclosure recessed and sealed to the cavity, is not considered a wall cavity.
source: ERAC · Battery Energy Storage System Installation Requirements (AS/NZS 5139:2019), published 2 Feb 2021, pp. 3-4

title: Other prohibited locations
text: A BESS must not be installed where a switchboard is prohibited (AS/NZS 3000:2018 clause 2.10.2.5), where a generation system is prohibited (clauses 6.2.4.7, 6.3.4.7, 6.4.4.7), or in locations prohibited by the manufacturer (refer to the manufacturer's installation instructions).
source: ERAC · Battery Energy Storage System Installation Requirements (AS/NZS 5139:2019), published 2 Feb 2021, p. 4

title: Appliances near a battery
text: Electrical appliances not associated with the BESS may not be located closer than 600 mm horizontally nor 900 mm above the BESS: e.g. heat pumps, air-conditioning equipment, hot water cylinders (gas and electric), motors, stoves, gas cooktops, stationary appliances. Solar power conversion equipment including inverters that supply a charge to the BESS are excluded. Switches, isolators and socket outlets are not considered electrical appliances.
source: ERAC · Battery Energy Storage System Installation Requirements (AS/NZS 5139:2019), published 2 Feb 2021, p. 4

title: Barrier behind the battery
text: When a BESS is on a wall, or on the ground within 300 mm of a wall, with a habitable room on the other side (bedrooms, study/home office, living rooms, kitchen/dining, playrooms, TV rooms, sunrooms), a non-combustible barrier is required behind it. Brick, masonry, concrete, compressed cement sheet and ceramic/clay tiles need no test; 6 mm cement sheet is industry best practice. Barrier must extend 600 mm beyond the sides and 900 mm above the BESS; if within 900 mm of the ceiling, the ceiling must be protected 600 mm past the BESS. Timber panels, plasterboard and particle board are not suitable. Openings over 5 mm must be sealed with fire-retardant sealant.
source: ERAC · Battery Energy Storage System Installation Requirements (AS/NZS 5139:2019), published 2 Feb 2021, pp. 4-5

title: Live electrical work
text: Electrical work, energised or de-energised, must only be carried out by appropriately licensed or registered electrical workers. A business must ensure electrical work is not carried out on equipment while it is energised, subject to narrow prescribed exceptions. Equipment must be tested to determine whether it is energised before work starts.
source: Safe Work Australia · Model Code of Practice: Managing electrical risks in the workplace (Oct 2018), section 4

title: We're AC coupling an existing solar inverter to a Deye three-phase hybrid and the site also needs zero export. Does Deye make a smart meter that takes 6 CTs, or do we need two meters? And how should the meter IDs be set?
text: Deye doesn't currently have a meter that takes 6 CTs. You can use two three-phase meters (3 CTs each), or one meter with 3 CTs for the AC-coupled inverter plus a separate set of 3 CTs (such as the CTs supplied in the inverter box) for zero export. The export-control (anti-backflow) meter must be set to address 01 and the AC-coupling meter (meter 2) to address 02.

title: What's the depth of discharge on the Deye AI-W5.1-B battery? Can we tell customers it's 100% usable?
text: Deye's recommended depth of discharge for the AI-W5.1-B is 90%. However, the stated usable energy is 5.12 kWh, which equals 100% of the 5.12 kWh nominal energy, measured at 0.5C charge and discharge at 25°C.

title: On a three-phase Deye hybrid with AC coupling, can meter 1 be a three-phase meter and meter 2 a single-phase meter? And can the existing inverter we're AC coupling be single-phase?
text: A three-phase Deye hybrid can only use three-phase meters. The existing inverter being AC coupled to the three-phase hybrid can be either single-phase or three-phase.

title: Are the Deye SUN series hybrid inverters (e.g. the 10kW models) covered by a 10-year warranty in Australia?
text: Yes. Deye confirmed these inverter models carry a 10-year warranty in Australia. The full terms are in Deye's 10-year limited warranty document for Australia and New Zealand.

title: On a Deye 10kW SG02 single-phase hybrid, which way should the grid CT arrow face? The app is showing a really high load and odd export.
text: On the 10kW SG02 inverter the CT arrow must point towards the grid. A reversed CT gives wrong load and export readings, so turn the CT around to face the grid and recheck the readings.

title: How do I connect a generator to a Deye 10kW single-phase hybrid? Which port does it go to, and does the GEN port need a specific plug?
text: A generator can be connected to the GEN port or the grid port. There's no specific plug on the inverter side: only the L and N wires need connecting at the GEN port, and any plug or inlet you fit depends on what the generator requires. The wiring diagram is in the user manual.

title: Why won't the Deye inverter let me set the battery's low SOC below 20%? I thought these batteries could go lower.
text: Low Batt can't be set lower than the Shutdown value. Lower the Shutdown setting first, then you can lower Low Batt.

title: Someone told me I should only charge my Deye battery between 10% and 90% to make it last longer. Is charging to 100% bad for it?
text: Deye batteries can be charged up to 100%. According to Deye, charging from 90% to 100% doesn't affect battery life.

title: The Deye WiFi logger won't connect to the customer's home WiFi, but it connects fine to a phone hotspot. The router's already on 2.4GHz. What else can we try?
text: Log into the customer's router, change the WiFi encryption to WPA2-PSK, then restart the router. Deye has fixed the same problem for other customers this way.

title: What does the W04 warning on a Deye hybrid inverter mean?
text: W04 is a meter communication fault. Check the meter communication cable and its pin connections between the meter and the inverter.

title: How do we lodge a warranty claim for a faulty Deye inverter, and what do we need to include?
text: Fill in Deye's warranty replacement form and send it to Deye's dedicated Australian service email. Include photos of the complete installation site, the damaged or faulty parts, the product serial number label and the inverter display, including any error messages. A video is preferred.

title: Does Deye sell brackets for mounting the batteries away from the wall, like putting one stack in front of another?
text: No. Deye doesn't currently supply fixtures for away-from-wall installation, and the manual only specifies the required clearances. If you install this way, the mounting structure must be fabricated locally and comply with applicable installation standards.

title: Do I need Time of Use turned on to run a Deye hybrid in self-consumption mode? We don't have time-of-use tariffs here in Queensland.
text: Yes. Time of Use must be enabled to get self-consumption, because that's the inverter's basic logic for it. If ToU is disabled, the battery is prevented from discharging at any time. Load First is a good option in most cases and is part of self-consumption.

title: Why would a 10kW three-phase Deye hybrid pull power from the grid when one phase has a 7kW load, even though the battery has plenty of charge?
text: A three-phase inverter's output is limited per phase. A 10kW unit is rated at roughly 4-5kW per phase, so if one phase's load exceeds that, the grid supplies the difference. Electricians set how loads are spread across phases when the property is built. To improve it, consider a larger inverter or paralleled inverters, because output rating is a hardware limit.

title: The load in the Deye app is showing a negative value. What does that mean?
text: A negative household or phase load usually means the CT is installed incorrectly: wrong clamp direction, wrong pin connection or wrong location. It has to be fixed on site.

title: Where do I set the CT ratio on a Deye system using an Eastron meter, and what should it be set to?
text: Set the CT ratio to match the rating printed on the CT label. With CTs wired directly to the inverter, set it on the inverter LCD or in the Deye app/Cloud. With an Eastron meter, set the ratio on the meter itself in its LCD setup mode. An incorrect ratio gives wrong power readings and can cause the battery to charge or discharge incorrectly.

title: What should the 'Batt' and 'Low Batt' SOC values be set to in Time of Use on a Deye hybrid?
text: The ToU 'Batt' value must not be lower than 'Low Batt', or the battery will malfunction. Try not to set Low Batt below 10%, or the battery may run completely flat. Deye recommends keeping the minimum SOC above about 10-15%, because a lower threshold risks over-discharge and shortens battery life.

title: What clearance do we need above a Deye battery? Is 300mm enough?
text: For the AI-W5.1-B there's no limit on clearance above the battery. For the Deye All-in-One unit, 300mm clearance above is required.

title: We're installing two Deye 12kW three-phase LV hybrids in parallel (master/slave). Do we need a meter or CT set for each inverter, or an extra meter to link them?
text: No. Paralleled inverters share a single set of grid meter/CTs, connected to the master inverter. CTs direct to the inverter are fine. An Eastron meter (SDM630 for three-phase) is only needed when the inverter is more than 10m from the main meter.

title: We want the battery to charge from the grid every day during the free-power window (11am to 2pm). How should Time of Use be set? And does the 'Power' value in ToU control how fast it charges?
text: Set the 11am-2pm ToU slot with Grid Charge ticked and the target SOC at 100%. All other hours run on self-consumption. The 'Power' value in ToU is the battery discharge power (its ability to supply the load), not the charging power. The charge rate comes from the battery's maximum charge current setting.

title: Can we get fault alerts from Deye Cloud for our customers' systems? And what does 'plant range' mean in the alert settings?
text: Yes. Both the plant owner and a business (installer) account with access to the plant can receive Deye Cloud app notifications for alerts. 'Plant range' is a business-account feature for choosing which plants you get alerts for. Select all if you want to monitor every site.

title: In the Deye app's work mode settings, what's the difference between Max Solar Power, Max Sell Power, ToU Power and GEN? And how should the Time of Use schedule be laid out?
text: Max Solar Power is the overall PV power limit, including power going to charge the battery. Max Sell Power is the export limit. ToU Power is the battery power limit, and GEN means generator charging of the battery. The ToU table is a single 24-hour day, not a 7-day schedule, and must run seamlessly from 12:00am to 11:59pm.

title: Can a single-phase generator be connected to a Deye 12kW three-phase hybrid inverter?
text: No. A three-phase Deye inverter can't be connected to a single-phase generator.

title: What's the difference between AC coupling an existing string inverter on the Deye's GEN port versus on the grid side, and what metering does each option need?
text: With GEN-port coupling, the existing inverter connects directly to the Deye's GEN port. Only one set of CTs on the grid incoming is needed and no extra energy meter, because the GEN port has internal sensors. The downside is that the existing inverter's output is capped by the Deye; the upside is that it can keep working as backup during an outage. Grid-side coupling uses a smart meter, and its pros and cons are the reverse.

title: We're getting a 'High DV voltage' error on a Deye 10kW hybrid. What causes it?
text: It means the DC voltage is too high. Check that the battery voltage and PV string voltage are within the inverter's range. In this case a PV reading of about 535V was considered too high, possibly because too many panels were connected on the string.

title: How often should my Deye battery be charged to 100%?
text: Charge the battery fully to 100% SOC at least once every two weeks. This keeps the SOC calibration accurate and the battery performing properly.

title: What is 'Smart Load' on a Deye hybrid, and what's a sensible way to set it?
text: Smart Load uses the GEN port as an output. It only receives power when the battery SOC and PV power are above thresholds you set. Setting it to switch on only at 100% SOC is quite restrictive; Deye suggests something like ON at 90%+ and OFF at 80%+.

title: What rating does the AC plug or connector need to be for a Deye 12kW three-phase hybrid (SUN-12K-SG04LP3)?
text: The SG04LP3-12K needs 17.4A per phase and 26.1A for pass-through. Choose a connector rated above the inverter's maximum operating current. It's a 5-pin connection (L1, L2, L3, N, PE). The final choice must comply with local electrical standards, and Deye doesn't specify third-party components.

title: With two Deye battery stacks, how do I tell which one is the master and which is the slave? What's the correct order to restart them?
text: The master is the stack using the PCS and OUT ports. To restart, turn both stacks off: press the power button first, then turn off the circuit breaker on the PDU. Turn the master on first (breaker on, then press the button), wait a while, then turn on the slave the same way.

title: When registering the LFDI in the Deye app for a site in Victoria on the Powercor network, which utility server should I select?
text: Select CPPALUE. It's used for CitiPower, Powercor and United Energy. If the device was previously registered under a different utility server, delete that registration first and then register again.

title: My SAJ app is showing the system in 'EMS mode'. What does that mean, and how do I turn it off?
text: EMS mode means the system is being controlled by a VPP (e.g. GloBird or Powston), so it may not behave as it would in self-consumption mode. It can't be switched off from the SAJ side; it is only an indication that the VPP is in control. As soon as the VPP releases the system, it changes back to self-consumption mode.

title: Can we put an SAJ three-phase hybrid inverter on a two-phase property?
text: No. On a two-phase property SAJ advise using a single-phase inverter with a three-phase smart meter, not a three-phase inverter.

title: How do we meter an SAJ H2 8kW single-phase hybrid that's being AC coupled to an existing grid-tied solar inverter?
text: Install it the same way as a hybrid system, but the SAJ needs to see the existing PV as well as the grid. Either fit two single-phase smart meters (and change the PV smart meter's address to 2), or fit one smart meter with two CTs, one on the grid and one on the existing PV output.

title: Do we need a second smart meter for an AC coupled SAJ system, and which meter setup do you recommend for single-phase and three-phase?
text: You can use a second meter, but SAJ's preferred option is one meter with 2 CTs for single phase, or one meter with 6 CTs for three phase. The single-phase one-CT meter that ships with the inverter is for DC coupled installs only.

title: The incoming mains on a job are 185mm parallel cables and we're putting in a 30kW SAJ hybrid. The standard CT won't fit. What CT and meter do we need?
text: The DTSU666 meter that comes with the inverter only suits CTs up to 100A. For larger cables you need to order a different smart meter from SAJ and source a suitably rated external split-core CT to clamp on the mains (SAJ gave a 1000A/5A split-core CT as an example), sized to the property's running current.

title: What export limit should an SAJ inverter be set to for the United Energy commissioning test?
text: For United Energy you can set the export limit to 0 or up to a maximum of 5 kW. SAJ support can also apply the settings remotely if you give them the inverter serial number and the NMI.

title: The SAJ inverter has no export limit set, but the system in South Australia still isn't exporting the way I expect. Why?
text: If the system is registered with SAPN as the DNSP, SAPN controls the system's export, even when no export limit is set on the inverter itself.

title: What's the minimum clearance above an SAJ hybrid inverter? Do we need 500mm, or can we go to 350mm? The job is in Brisbane.
text: The CEC guideline is 900mm from the top of a battery system (inverter plus battery) to the roof. In Brisbane there's generally no inspection requirement, so it may be possible to go below that. SAJ recommend at least 500mm above the inverter for ventilation, and it can be as little as 300mm if needed, but keep the largest gap you can for cooling.

title: What's the minimum gap between SAJ battery stacks? Is that measured battery to battery or cover to cover?
text: The minimum is 200mm between stacks, measured from the battery cover, since the battery ends where the cover ends. SAJ recommend keeping at least 300mm or more for ventilation and easier maintenance access.

title: We're installing 2 x 10kW SAJ single-phase hybrids, each with 3 battery modules, and there's no existing solar. How do we connect them? Does it matter if the property is single phase or two phase?
text: On a single-phase property you need an SAJ eManager to link the two systems so they work in parallel (assuming no third-party inverter). On a two-phase property with no existing system, you can install one system on each phase, with one smart meter on each phase.

title: We're struggling to pass the AusNet commissioning (export) test on an SAJ battery system. What conditions does the system need to be in to pass?
text: The system has to actually export during the test, so run it on a good sunny day with PV of at least around 2 kW and household load lower than PV. The battery should be charged enough, or turned off or stopped by SAJ, so PV isn't just charging it, and any VPP control has to be removed first. If it fails at the export step, ask the customer to reduce their load and re-run. The NMI must also be registered with AusNet and linked to the inverter's LFDI.

title: What's the usable capacity and depth of discharge of the SAJ battery with 6.4kWh modules, and how many modules can go in a stack on single-phase and three-phase inverters?
text: DoD is 100%, so usable capacity equals total capacity: each module is 6.4kWh, ranging from 12.8kWh (2 modules) to 51.2kWh (8 modules). The theoretical minimum SOC is 0%, but the BMS applies a practical protection SOC in operation. Stacks are 2-6 modules on single-phase inverters and 3-8 modules on three-phase, and the H2-(10-30)K-T3 needs at least 4 modules.

title: My SAJ app shows a 'battery open circuit' fault. What does that mean?
text: A battery open circuit fault means the battery has been turned off, or hasn't been commissioned yet. Turn the battery back on and reboot the system. If it isn't commissioned, the installer needs to finish that on site.

title: How do I stop an SAJ battery discharging to the house between midnight and 6am so the home runs off the grid then?
text: Use Time of Use mode and set the discharge power to 0 W for the period you don't want the battery to discharge (e.g. 12am-6am). The house will draw from the grid during that window.

title: After an SAJ install, the batteries just sit on standby and won't charge or discharge, and load shows zero. What setting should we check first?
text: Check the meter setting. If it's set to 'no meter', the inverter can't read load and the battery won't charge or discharge properly. Set it to match the meter actually installed and whether the system is DC or AC coupled, and confirm grid compliance has been set too. If a 'lost communication' error appears after setting the meter, the smart meter wiring or communication needs checking.

title: Why does my SAJ Elekeeper app show much lower grid import than my energy retailer's app or bill?
text: Elekeeper reports load and import based on where the smart meter is installed. If the meter is on the main incoming supply and no load bypasses it, readings should be accurate. If any load bypasses the smart meter, the app won't capture that consumption, so the installation needs to be checked for bypassed loads.

title: When registering an SAJ system for the DNSP, we're getting 'NMI bind failed'. What does that mean?
text: 'NMI bind failed' means the NMI has already been used or bound. Contact the distributor (DNSP) to get it released, then try again.

title: My customers say their new SAJ Elekeeper accounts show as not registered. Is something wrong with the app?
text: Make sure the International node (server) is selected when registering or logging in. The app may default to the European node, and selecting International has fixed the same issue for other customers.

title: What does an isolation (insulation) fault on an SAJ inverter mean? Is it a DC or AC side problem?
text: It means unwanted electrical leakage to earth. In most cases it comes from the DC side (PV panels or cables), but it can also come from the AC side, so check both. Common causes are damaged DC cables, water ingress in connectors or junction boxes, faulty panels, loose connections and moisture after rain. Note whether it appears after rain, have the installer do an insulation resistance test, and inspect cables, connectors and panels on site.

title: My SAJ system is showing a 'lost communication' error. What does it mean and what should I do?
text: Lost communication means the inverter doesn't have a stable connection with the smart meter. First check that the smart meter is powered on. If it is, an installer needs to visit the site and call SAJ from site to fix it.

title: An SAJ three-phase inverter is showing a 'grid phase sequence' alarm. Can it be fixed remotely?
text: No. A grid phase sequence fault needs a site visit to correct the wiring. Ask the installer to call SAJ support from site so the team can help.

title: We replaced a faulty SAJ inverter under warranty. Does SAJ reimburse the installer's labour or callout, and how do we claim it?
text: SAJ pay $150 plus GST per inverter replacement. Send SAJ an invoice for each replaced inverter with its serial number so it can be reimbursed, and SAJ will arrange collection of the faulty units.

title: We're installing a SOFAR HYD 10KTL-3PH with battery on a three-phase home that already has a 10kW grid-tied inverter from another brand. How do we get the existing system's production into the SOFAR monitoring? Does SOFAR have an AC-coupling meter option?
text: SOFAR's AC-coupling solution uses two meters: the one supplied in the inverter box plus one extra meter purchased separately. Either CT-type or inline meters work, and either can be used for PV monitoring or grid monitoring. The PV meter's address must be changed to 2 so it is distinguished from the grid meter.

title: Can we AC couple a SOFAR HYD or ESI inverter and battery onto a property that already has another system? What if the existing system already has a battery?
text: Yes, but only when the existing system is a PV-only (grid-tied) inverter. You must never AC couple onto an existing battery system: two battery systems from different brands can't work on one site, because each needs its own CT/meter at the same point and they give conflicting grid/consumption readings. A solar-only site with no battery can have a SOFAR HYD/ESI and SOFAR batteries AC coupled.

title: Are SOFAR BTS batteries high voltage or low voltage, and how many can go on a HYD 15KTL-3PH? Can I fit 5 in one stack, or get 50kWh on a 15kW or 20kW inverter?
text: BTS is a high-voltage battery. Each stack takes a maximum of 4 batteries, so 5 in one stack isn't possible. The HYD 15kW three-phase has two battery channels, so it can take up to 2 stacks of 4 (8 batteries total). 50kWh is not possible on the 15kW or 20kW models; the maximum is 40kWh.

title: How much clearance do I need above a SOFAR BTS battery stack: 300mm or 900mm?
text: SOFAR's own standard clearance above the battery is 300-600mm. However, in Australia you may need to follow AS/NZS 5139, which requires 900mm to the ceiling for indoor installs.

title: Can a SOFAR inverter and battery system be installed outdoors? What do installers usually put underneath the battery as a base?
text: Yes. The SOFAR inverter is IP65 rated and can be installed outdoors, but SOFAR suggests a rain shelter if it isn't under the eaves. For the battery base, SOFAR commonly sees bricks or pavers used.

title: My SOFAR inverter keeps stopping because the grid voltage is around 260-261V. Can you raise or turn off the voltage limit so it keeps producing?
text: No. The inverter is set to the 260V upper limit, which is the maximum allowed in Australia, and it can't be disabled because of AS/NZS 4777 and CEC rules. When grid voltage is above this the inverter will stop. The fix is on the network side, so speak to the network operator about the grid transformer voltage.

title: Can the depth of discharge on my SOFAR batteries be set to 95% so I get more out of them?
text: No. The maximum depth of discharge SOFAR allows is 90%, so it can be set to 90% but not 95%.

title: My SOFAR inverter is showing an 'AC voltage lost' alarm. Can it be restarted remotely, and what should be checked?
text: Generally a reboot won't fix an 'AC voltage lost' alarm. First check whether the inverter's AC switch or breaker has tripped. If not, check the AC side for normal voltage: if voltage is present, the inverter's AC voltage sampling sensor may be faulty; if there's no voltage, check everything on the AC side to find out why.

title: Is there a wiring diagram and settings for running two SOFAR ESI 5K-S1-A inverters in parallel as master and slave?
text: Connect the master's link port 0 to the slave's link port 1. Set the DIP switch to 'ON' for an empty link port and to '1' for a connected port. On each inverter screen go to Menu > Advanced Settings > password 0001/0715 > Parallel Control > Enable, then set the master/leader to address 00 and the slave/follower to address 01.

title: I've set my SOFAR system to charge from the grid between 11am and 2pm using TOU mode. How do I also set a discharge period?
text: TOU mode can only charge. To discharge as well, use Timing mode, which allows both charge and discharge periods. Make sure the time periods don't overlap.

title: How do I register a SOFAR inverter for CSIP and get the LFDI in Solarman for a Victorian network commissioning test?
text: First check that the inverter firmware has been updated to the CSIP encrypted version. Then in the Solarman Business portal go to Application > Device Registration, fill in the details and generate the LFDI. Once that succeeds, you can run the test.

title: Where do I set the export limit on a SOFAR inverter? Can it be done in the Solarman app?
text: The export limit can't be set from the app. Set it on site on the inverter screen under Menu > Advanced Settings > Feed-in Limit, or SOFAR support can change it remotely.

title: Does SOFAR make an AC-coupled battery inverter that works with the BTS 5K batteries? I thought there was an ME3000.
text: SOFAR has no pure AC-coupled inverter. Both the HYD (three-phase, split) and ESI (single-phase all-in-one) hybrids can do AC coupling, and both use the BTS 5K battery, which is the only battery at this stage. The ME3000 has been phased out and hasn't been on the CEC list for a long time.

title: On a SOFAR system with a single CT, where exactly should the CT be clamped? The load reading just seems to follow the solar production.
text: If consumption is following PV production, the CT is most likely clamped in the wrong position rather than just pointing the wrong way. The CT must clamp on the incoming mains, between the service fuse and the main switch, with the arrow pointing towards the grid.
